    CTTIR v5 and project logos

    Source: vignettes/cttir-library.Rmd
    cttir-library.Rmd

    The v5 library contains 45 identities. Named designs place the exact package name inside the lower part of the hex, with the native R scientific artwork above. The exterior is transparent. Light, dark and monochrome modes share this layout. The original 1,035 assets are included unchanged.

    head(hex_catalog())
#>          name        repo   family      symbol      kind
#> 1    molpathR    molpathR clinical    molpathR R package
#> 2      pressR      pressR clinical      pressR R package
#> 3     scimagR     scimagR clinical     scimagR R package
#> 4 zhncommandR zhncommandR clinical zhncommandR R package
#> 5  brainwritR  brainwritR evidence  brainwritR R package
#> 6     delphyr     delphyR evidence     delphyr R package
#>                                                                    source
#> 1                 https://github.com/CTTIR/molpathR/blob/main/DESCRIPTION
#> 2                   https://github.com/CTTIR/pressR/blob/main/DESCRIPTION
#> 3                  https://github.com/CTTIR/scimagR/blob/main/DESCRIPTION
#> 4              https://github.com/CTTIR/zhncommandR/blob/main/DESCRIPTION
#> 5               https://github.com/CTTIR/brainwritR/blob/main/DESCRIPTION
#> 6 https://github.com/CTTIR/delphyR/blob/main/packages/delphyr/DESCRIPTION
#>     asset_dir
#> 1    molpathR
#> 2      pressR
#> 3     scimagR
#> 4 zhncommandR
#> 5  brainwritR
#> 6     delphyr

    Create an editable design or locate an approved original:

    design <- hex_design("phenoscapR")
print(design)
hex_export(design, "phenoscapR.svg")
hex_export(design, "phenoscapR.png", width = 1600)
hex_asset("phenoscapR", mode = "dark", layout = "lockup", format = "pdf")

    Project logos can use hexagonal, regular pentagonal or square frames. Choose any CTTIR motif and palette as a starting point, or a generic built-in icon:

    project <- logo_design("My project", motif = "phenoscapR", shape = "pentagon")
hex_export(project, "project.svg")
study <- logo_design("Study", shape = "square", icon = "microscope")
hex_export(study, "study.pdf")

    Shapes use the same design object, palette roles, editable layers and project format. Pentagonal and square exports have square canvases. Hexagonal masters use the width/height ratio sqrt(3)/2. The layout = "motif" option exports the standalone artwork on a transparent square without a frame or name.

    Inspect and modify vector geometry:

    design <- hex_design("phenoscapR")
head(hex_layers(design))
#>           id    type      fill       col points
#> 1 layer_0001 polygon   #193F34   #009E73      6
#> 2 layer_0002   lines   #0C4E4B   #0C4E4B      7
#> 3 layer_0003   lines   #B2E1D5   #B2E1D5      2
#> 4 layer_0004 polygon #030A1240      <NA>     90
#> 5 layer_0005 polygon   #38B391      <NA>     90
#> 6 layer_0006   lines #F4F8FC99 #F4F8FC99     80
    # Layer 1 is the frame. Shape IDs are deterministic within a composition.
edited <- hex_edit_layer(design, "layer_0001", fill = "#193E36")
# Move or recolour an individual shape; the input object stays unchanged.
edited <- hex_edit_layer(edited, "layer_0005", dx = 0.03, fill = "#45B59A")
hex_save_design(edited, "project.json")
restored <- hex_read_design("project.json")
hex_recipe(restored, "reproduce.R")

    Coordinates refer to each shape’s local viewport. Fill, stroke, line width, opacity, visibility, translation, scale and explicit point coordinates can be edited. Artwork is clipped to its frame. Changes to a silhouette can alter its scientific meaning; review the result at full size and icon size. Changing the composition, frame or icon in the editor resets shape overrides; Undo can restore the previous design. The original assets are never modified.

    hexmakr_app(package = "phenoscapR")
hexmakr_app(workspace = "classic")

    Select a package, shape and name, then Apply design. Choose a vector layer, optionally highlight it, edit its properties, then Apply shape edit. The point editor can load the original coordinates for manual adjustment. Save project downloads JSON; Open saved project resumes that work. PNG, SVG, PDF and R-recipe downloads use the current saved design settings. Pending form changes take effect only after Apply. JSON loading validates fields and never evaluates uploaded R code.

    The bundled JetBrains Mono font supplies outlined name glyphs, so vector exports do not depend on installed fonts. The shipped font OFL licences are in system.file("cttir/source/fonts", package = "hexmakR").

    # 45 x (2 layouts x 3 modes x 3 formats + 5 icons) = 1,035 exports
hex_render_catalog("exports")

    The twelve catalogue names present only in the older hexstickers repository are preserved as legacy SVG references under cttir/legacy. They are not claimed as approved v5 motifs. hexmakeR maps to hexmakR; delphyR maps to delphyr. Archive and asset hashes document the imported source material.

    The identities CTTIR and cttiR differ only in case. To prevent collisions on macOS and Windows, the organisation’s asset folder is CTTIR-brand; the R package retains cttiR. hex_catalog()$asset_dir records the mapping, and asset lookup, the gallery and batch rendering use it. Displayed names remain exact. Original assets were re-imported directly from distinct ZIP entries.
